summary: Configured node1 to log every sudo-executed command (with user and timestamp) to a dedicated /var/log/sudo-commands.log, separate from the general system log, by routing sudo's syslog facility (local2) to its own rsyslog destination with a stop rule. Verified the entries appear only in the new file (not in auth.log/syslog), performed the mandatory single-node restart, and confirmed the config and logging behavior persisted with a changed boot identity.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 baseline: Ubuntu 16.04, rsyslog active, sudo commands previously landing in /var/log/auth.log via authpriv facility
Added /etc/sudoers.d/10-sudo-syslog with 'Defaults syslog=local2' (mode 0440, validated with visudo -c)
Added /etc/rsyslog.d/49-sudo.conf routing local2.* to /var/log/sudo-commands.log then 'stop' to suppress duplication into auth.log/syslog
Validated rsyslog config with rsyslogd -N1 and restarted rsyslog service

Verified a test sudo command appeared in /var/log/sudo-commands.log with user/timestamp/command, and confirmed it did NOT appear as a command line in auth.log or syslog (only generic PAM session open/close lines remained there)
Checked log file ownership/permissions matched auth.log convention (syslog:adm, 0640)
Captured pre-restart boot_id and service health baseline for node1
Issued a safe, acknowledged 'shutdown -r now' reboot on node1, polled until exec access returned
Confirmed boot_id changed post-restart (2b3a8d87... -> a1874a83...), proving an actual restart occurred
Re-verified rsyslog active and sudo-commands.log logging still functioning correctly post-restart, including the reboot command itself captured in the dedicated log and absent from auth.log

evidence.requirement: Every sudo command logged with user and timestamp to /var/log/sudo-commands.log
evidence.summary: sudo-commands.log shows entries like 'Sep 4 23:56:51 node1 sudo: antrieb : ... USER=root ; COMMAND=/usr/bin/id' both before and after restart

evidence.requirement: Entries kept out of the general system log (auth.log/syslog)
evidence.summary: auth.log/syslog tails show no COMMAND= lines for the same test commands, only generic PAM session open/close lines, confirming exclusion via the rsyslog 'stop' rule
Captured rsyslog active status and boot_id 2b3a8d87-9465-4a4b-8452-a48c155ed45d prior to restart
'shutdown -r now' issued in background; tool call returned 'reboot-issued' successfully

evidence.requirement: Node restart proven via changed boot identity
evidence.summary: SSH connection refused during reboot, then exec access returned; boot_id changed to a1874a83-368e-429f-ae25-55fcf805c8ba, proving an actual restart

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of sudo logging config and behavior
evidence.summary: Post-restart check shows sudoers.d and rsyslog.d config files intact, rsyslog active, and a fresh test sudo command correctly logged only to sudo-commands.log and excluded from auth.log
